statement: Two squares, each with sides of 3 cm, are put side by side to make a rectangle. How long is the line all the way around the rectangle?

choices.misconception: I gave the length of the rectangle, 3 + 3, not the distance all the way around it.
I found the distance around one square only.
I added 12 cm for each square and took away the side where they touch only once.
I added the distance around both squares, so I counted the sides where they touch.

hints: Draw the rectangle. Which sides are on the outside?
Draw the two squares joined together. The sides where they touch are now inside the rectangle, so walk around the outside only and add up each side you pass.
The rectangle is 3 + 3 = 6 cm long and 3 cm tall. Add the long side, the short side, the long side and the short side.

solutions.reliable: Side by side, the two squares make a rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm tall. Going all the way round: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 cm. The idea to keep: the distance around a shape counts only the outside edges, never the lines inside it.
solutions.elegant: Going round the rectangle you walk along 6 sides of the small squares, each 3 cm long, so the distance is 6 x 3 = 18 cm.

whyOnTest: Joining shapes hides the sides where they touch, so this checks that a child measures only the outside edge.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
